evidence: Integrity: environment/assets/seed_data.json and solution/app/src/seed_data.json both hash a1c65c806b54da99a37ab2b5f455ede0a9385a09569903fb3a7f3446f7e83740, matching manifest.json; the only shipped data file besides package.json; it parses. Dockerfile 'COPY assets/ /assets/'. Programmatic check (in-memory Python script kept in temp, run with -I -B) over every record: 10 user ids, 3 job ids and 16 application ids are unique; no duplicate user email; every job recruiter_id has role recruiter and manager_id role hiring_manager; interview_limit 3/2/3 within 1-50 (rules sec.2); every application job_id and stage resolves; positions are contiguous 1..n in every (job,stage); Interview occupancy 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 so no limit is pre-violated (rules 'Interview never holds more cards than ...'); only APP-301 is REJECTED and it alone carries rejected_from=SCREEN (a valid pre-reject stage) and a non-blank reject_reason; no job has the same email twice (Noor on JOB-PLAT and JOB-DSGN is allowed: 'one person can apply to several jobs'); each candidate account's email maps to its applications with matching names (CAN1->APP-101,APP-302; CAN2->APP-201; CAN3->APP-301). All 127 messages resolve application_id and sender_id, and every sender is authorized under rules sec.6 (recruiters; candidate senders own the application); no blank body; per-thread timestamps strictly increasing and unique; APP-101 has 120 messages, matching app_context 'Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation is long (120 messages at the start)'. All 3 notes resolve and authors are allowed (MGR1 on own JOB-PLAT, REC1, MGR3 on own JOB-DSGN). All 6 read markers resolve, 1<=read_count<=thread length (golden db.js:82-83 indexes read_count-1, so no 0 marker is needed). Derived state agrees with criteria: Lena (CAN3, marker 2 of 3, message 3 by REC3) has exactly 1 unread, matching hro_unread_counts 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread'; JOB-DATA manager is Bill (USR-MGR2), matching hro_seen. stages and candidate_status_labels equal the rules sec.7 table; thread_page_size 30 matches rules sec.6. Cleanliness: all emails use RFC 2606 reserved .example domains (hireops.example 7, candidates.example 7, mail.example 12); names are ordinary synthetic names with no phone, address, DOB or ID numbers; no non-ASCII; a regex scan for <, >, javascript:, http, ${, {{, 'ignore', 'prompt', 'password', 'secret', 'token', api key, SQL comment and sk- hit only benign words ('systems', 'Finance Systems', '/instructions/' in generated_note). No credential or password is in the seed (the shared demo password Hireops!2026 lives in instruction.md/app_context, which the profile and the Internal annotation permit; golden db.js inserts a hashed pw). Golden seeds once ('A database that already holds users is never reseeded'). Lessons file reviewed: its patterns (hidden requirements, public addresses, timing races, restart checks, double grading) do not bear on seed content; no public URL or probe-like literal is in the seed. Raw evidence index hashes for workspace.cjs and results/workspace.json recomputed and match; that evidence is scripted golden observation only and is not needed for this source-level row. Broken-app/alternative probe: a conforming app reading read_count literally as 'messages read from the first' (rules sec.9) gets the criterion-stated values; an app that naively computes unread = total - read_count would show a false unread to Noor (marker 119, message 120 is her own) and Farah (REC3 marker 2, message 3 her own) a false unread, which the public rule 'My own messages are never unread for me' correctly penalizes, so this is a fair, publicly stated edge rather than a seed inconsistency.
notes: Minor observation (not a defect): USR-CAN1 on APP-101 and USR-REC3 on APP-301 each sent the last message of their thread yet hold a read marker one below it, whereas the runtime rule says 'sending a message counts as reading the conversation'. Under the public unread and seen rules every derived count and seen state is identical either way (own messages never unread; seen depends on the other side's marker), so no grading outcome changes; it reads as a deliberate check of the own-message rule. generated_note points to /instructions/, which is unavailable at runtime, but it is metadata text only.
